quizzes.title: Penal and Council Provisions: MCQ
quizzes.passage: The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 was enacted after the Supreme Court's judgment in NALSA vs Union of India, which recognised transgender people as a third gender and granted them legal recognition and rights. The 2019 Act was passed to provide protection of rights of transgender persons and their welfare. The government has now presented the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026 in the Lok Sabha to revise that Act. The Bill narrows the definition of transgender person and removes some categories, including trans-man, trans-woman and genderqueer. It also makes the penal framework stronger by expanding penal provisions. The offences it covers include forced mutilation of minors and the forcing of children into begging. The Bill requires medical institutions to report gender-affirming surgeries to an official authority. Under the Bill, certificate holders are allowed to change their name in official documents. The Bill further revises the composition of the National Council for Transgender Persons. The Bill's proposals have drawn both support and criticism, with critics pointing to the earlier Supreme Court judgment and supporters pointing to the aim of welfare. Its changes affect the penal, reporting and naming provisions of the law. These changes are discussed alongside the wider significance of the Bill.

questions.q: Who nominates the members of the National Council for Transgender Persons under the Bill?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the members are nominated by the Centre Government.

questions.q: What is the maximum imprisonment the Bill prescribes for forcing children into begging?
questions.explanation: The booklet states up to 14 years imprisonment for forcing children into begging.

questions.q: Which punishment does the Bill prescribe for forced mutilation of minors?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists life imprisonment as the punishment for forced mutilation of minors.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The National Council for Transgender Persons is to include representatives of States and Union Territories.
Reason (R): Representation on the National Council is to be rotational across regions.
options: A is true, but R is false.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation: The booklet lists both points separately, and rotational representation does not explain the inclusion of States and UTs.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Forced mutilation of minors   ->   A. Life imprisonment
II. Forcing children into begging   ->   B. Up to 14 years
III. Reporting of gender-affirming surgeries   ->   C. District Magistrate
IV. Nomination of Council members   ->   D. Central Government
questions.explanation: Each item in List I matches its penalty, reporting authority or nominating authority as stated in the booklet.

questions.q:
Read the following statements:
I. Medical institutions must report gender-affirming surgeries to the District Magistrate.
II. Forcing children into begging can attract up to 14 years of imprisonment.
III. Members of the National Council are nominated by State Governments.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while statement III is wrong because the Centre nominates the members.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
Life imprisonment is prescribed for forced mutilation of minors.
Forcing children into begging attracts up to 14 years of imprisonment.
Members of the National Council are nominated by State Governments.
questions.explanation: The first two statements are correct, and the third is wrong because the Centre nominates the members.

questions.q: Under the Bill, up to how many years of imprisonment can be imposed for forcing children into begging? (number of years)

questions.q: To which authority must medical institutions report gender-affirming surgeries? (two words)

quizzes.title: Significance and Criticism: MCQ
quizzes.passage: The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 was passed to provide protection of rights of transgender persons and their welfare. The NALSA judgment in 2014 recognised transgender people as a third gender, and that recognition forms part of the background to the debate. The Union Government has now presented an Amendment Bill, 2026 in the Lok Sabha to revise that Act. The Bill narrows the definition of transgender person and makes the penal framework stronger by expanding penal provisions. Under the Bill, a Medical Board led by a Chief Medical Officer or Deputy CMO would verify transgender identity, and certificate holders could change their name in official documents. The Bill has drawn both support and criticism in public debate. Supporters argue that the Bill is meant to improve welfare for transgender persons. They also point out that mandatory reporting can support national planning for healthcare and welfare schemes. Critics question the Bill's approach and raise several concerns about it. They say that the verification process raises questions of its own. They also raise other concerns about the proposals, and they warn that some broad legal terms could be misused. The debate therefore covers welfare, certification, reporting and the wording of the law.

questions.q: According to the booklet, what effect do Medical Boards have on the discretionary power of District Magistrates?
options: They increase the discretionary power of District Magistrates
They reduce the discretionary power of District Magistrates
They replace District Magistrates in issuing certificates entirely
They have no connection with District Magistrates
questions.explanation: The booklet says Medical Board-based certification reduces the discretionary power of District Magistrates.

questions.q: Which offences does the Bill's penal framework address, according to the booklet?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the stronger penal framework addresses mutilation, abduction and forced identity.

questions.q: Under the Bill, broad terms such as 'Inducement' or 'Allurement' could be used against which two groups?
questions.explanation: The booklet warns that such broad terms could be used against NGOs and healthcare providers.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Removing self-identification from the 2019 Act is seen as contrary to the NALSA judgment.
Reason (R): The NALSA judgment recognised gender identity as a Fundamental Right under Article 21.
options: A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: The booklet says removal of self-identification contradicts NALSA, which recognised gender identity as a Fundamental Right under Article 21.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Verification by Medical Board   ->   A. May pathologise gender identity
II. Mandatory reporting of surgeries   ->   B. May violate medical confidentiality
III. Narrow definition of transgender person   ->   C. Aims to ensure benefits reach the most marginalised
IV. Terms like 'Inducement' or 'Allurement'   ->   D. May restrict voluntary gender transition support
questions.explanation: Each item in List I matches the concern the booklet attaches to it.

questions.q:
Read the following points about the Bill:
I. The narrower definition is intended to direct welfare to the most marginalised communities.
II. The removal of self-identification is consistent with the NALSA judgment.
III. Medical Board verification may pathologise gender identity.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while statement II is wrong because the booklet says removal contradicts NALSA.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
Mandatory reporting of surgeries may violate medical confidentiality and personal privacy.
The NALSA judgment recognised gender identity as a statutory right.
The penal framework addresses abduction.
questions.explanation: The first and third statements are correct, and the second is wrong because NALSA recognised gender identity as a Fundamental Right.

quizzes.title: Significance and Criticism: TITA
quizzes.passage: The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026 has drawn both support and criticism. Supporters say the Bill aims to make welfare more targeted, and they point out that a narrower definition can help focus benefits. They also say that certification based on verification reduces the discretionary power of District Magistrates. According to supporters, mandatory reporting can help build a national record for planning healthcare and welfare schemes. They also note that the penal framework addresses serious crimes. Critics say that the Bill departs from an earlier Supreme Court judgment, which recognised rights for transgender persons. Critics also argue that the verification process raises concerns about how transgender people are assessed. They raise concerns about the reporting of certain procedures, and they warn that broad language in the Bill could be used against groups working in the sector. Such language, critics say, may also restrict support that people give voluntarily to those seeking transition-related help. The Bill also removes some categories from the definition of transgender person, and it changes the way such persons obtain certificates. The debate covers several parts of the Bill, including its penal, certification and reporting provisions. The Bill proposes changes to several parts of the law.

questions.q: In which year did the NALSA vs Union of India judgment come? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the NALSA vs Union of India judgment to 2014.

questions.q: Which term, listed alongside 'Allurement', is described as a broad term that could be misused? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet names 'Inducement' and 'Allurement' as broad terms that could be used against NGOs and healthcare providers.

questions.q: According to critics, verification may do what to a person's gender? (one word)
questions.explanation: Critics say Medical Board verification may pathologise gender identity.

questions.q: Mandatory reporting of surgeries may violate which kind of confidentiality? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says mandatory surgery reporting may violate medical confidentiality and personal privacy.

questions.q: The penal framework addresses mutilation, abduction and forced ___. (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the penal framework addresses mutilation, abduction and forced identity.

questions.q: The narrower definition aims to ensure that benefits reach which kind of communities? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the narrow definition aims to ensure benefits reach the most marginalised communities.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution did the NALSA judgment recognise a Fundamental Right for transgender persons? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the NALSA judgment recognised gender identity as a Fundamental Right under Article 21.
